Article Title: No government role, don’t endorse Hasina’s remarks at private media event: MEA
Article Text:
The Bangladesh foreign ministry had said this interaction by a “convicted mass murderer” on the Indian soil stood as an affront to the sovereignty of the country

NEW DELHI: With former Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina ’s news conference kicking up a diplomatic firestorm, the government said on Friday her remarks, especially those related to the government in Dhaka, are not endorsed by India.“Government had no role to play in what was an event by a private media entity, and the government does not endorse anything said at the forum, especially with regard to the duly constituted govt of Bangladesh,” said ministry of external affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal.Following this, Bangladesh had expressed outrage over the former PM’s remarks, saying the event had hurt the sentiments of its people and could adversely affect efforts to improve bilateral ties with India.The Bangladesh foreign ministry had said this interaction by a “convicted mass murderer” on the Indian soil stood as an affront to the sovereignty of the country and that Bangladesh would never be a client state.
Article Summary: The bangladesh foreign ministry had said this interaction by a “convicted mass murderer’ on the indian soil stood as an affront to the sovereignty of the country. “government had no role to play in what was an event by a private media entity,” said ministry of external affairs spokesperson randhir jaiswal.

Article Title: UPI charges: Lok Sabha passes bill for government to make changes
Article Text:
The FM said the charge will apply to merchants and not to users and will help banks and fintech invest in infrastructure and innovation

NEW DELHI: The Lok Sabha on Thursday passed a Bill that seeks to ease tax rules to attract investments and remove the existing legal provision that prevents banks and payment service providers from charging Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on notified electronic payment modes.The Bill — passed without discussion amid din — also proposes to remove the linkage between the Payment and Settlement Systems Act and the I-Tax Act and give legal backing to the government to modify the zero-MDR framework on UPI and RuPay card transactions. Outside the House, however, there was an exchange between FM Nirmala Sitharaman and Congress MP Jairam Ramesh. Ramesh said the Bill opens the doors for MDR. The FM responded, saying the charge will apply to merchants and not to users and will help banks and fintech invest in infrastructure and innovation.“More importantly, the UPI and services steering committee headed by NPCI is yet to decide on the MDR. This will happen after Parliament passes the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026... All this could have been discussed on the floor of the House if your party @INCIndia (Congress) engages constructively in Parliament when the Bill was/is tabled,” she said.While leaving person-to-payments outside MDR’s ambit, banks and fintechs may be permitted to charge 0.25% to 0.4% on payments to businesses in excess of Rs 2,000 with an overall ceiling on how much can be charged.Officials have argued that the levy will be lower than what is charged on credit and debit cards, and most merchants will not pass it on to consumers.
Article Summary: The bill also proposes to remove the linkage between the payment and settlement systems act and the i-tax act. Outside the house, there was an exchange between fm nirmala sitharaman and congress mp jairam ramesh. The fm said the charge will apply to merchants and not to users.

Article Title: Government maps 27 Arunachal border locations with standard names
Article Text:
Several of the named sites on the map carry the weight of India-China conflict.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

GUWAHATI/NEW DELHI: The updated Survey of India map has assigned standard place and feature names to 27 Arunachal Pradesh sites, including four mountain passes and a high-altitude lake, as part of the Union government’s strategy to remove any ambiguity on demarcation of territory and counter China’s repeated attempts to rename places on this side of the McMahon Line.The MHA said on Friday that the names were finalised in consultation with the Arunachal Pradesh government. “Identifying them formally on the Survey of India map is aimed at facilitating their accurate recognition and better awareness among the public.”Of the 27 sites identified on the map, one is a monument. Three of the rest — Longju, Maja & Bisa — are strategically important border villages in Upper Subansiri district. There are also three passes along the McMahon Line, Dzo La, Riza La and Pukur La, in the same district. Thag La pass, a 1962 battleground, lies on the border in Tawang district.“These places are already marked on Indian military maps, even those of 1962 vintage. Identifying them on Survey of India maps is a bold counter to China,” a source said.Several of the named sites carry the weight of India-China conflict. Longju was one of the earliest flashpoints in the boundary dispute and was occupied by Chinese troops in 1959.Thag La overlooks Namka Chu valley, where the 1962 conflict began after Chinese forces crossed the McMahon Line.Jaswant Garh, in Tawang, commemorates Rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat, one of the most celebrated heroes of 1962 war. The Sher-e-Thapa Memorial in Upper Subansiri honours Hav Shere Thapa, whose resistance at Rio Bridge significantly delayed the Chinese advance in 1962. The lone lake named is Sambho Sarovar, a high-altitude glacial lake.The remaining land areas include Bara Kundun, Chhota Kundun and Dhan Bari in Anjaw district; Pritnagar, Buddhamandir, Jairampur, Teritnagar and Ramnagar in Changlang; Sagar, Padma, Jyotinagar and Baisakhi in West Kameng; Chhota Ropuk and Bara Ropuk in Upper Subansiri; and Shivaji Nagar, Sunpura and Kamlang Nagar in Lohit.In April, China announced Chinese names for 23 locations in Arunachal Pradesh, which Beijing refers to as “South Tibet”. The external affairs ministry then said assigning “fictitious names” wouldn’t alter the reality that Arunachal Pradesh “was, is, and will always remain an integral and inalienable part of India”. China has carried out similar renaming exercises periodically.McMahon Line demarcates the boundary between India and China in the eastern sector, separating Arunachal from Tibet.
Article Summary: The updated survey of india map has assigned standard place and feature names to 27 arunachal pradesh sites, including four mountain passes and a high-altitude lake. It is part of the union government’s strategy to remove any ambiguity on demarcation of territory. China has repeated attempts to rename places on this side of the mcmahon line.

Article Title: 'Fake news, AI-generated': MEA dismisses report of India requesting defence pact with Israel after Mecca agreement
Article Text:
MEA has dismissed as “fake news” a report claiming India sought a defence pact with Israel after the Pakistan-Saudi-Turkey security agreement.

With inputs from ANI

NEW DELHI: The Ministry of External Affairs on Friday rejected a report claiming India had approached Israel for a defence pact following the signing of a new security agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey. The ministry called the claim “fake news” generated using artificial intelligence.The report, published by Turkish outlet Straturka and subsequently circulated on social media, claimed that New Delhi had initiated discussions with Tel Aviv to counter the emerging Pakistan-Saudi-Turkey security arrangement. The report cited unnamed Pakistani sources.The MEA’s Fact Check unit shared a screenshot of the report on X and flagged it as fake, warning users against what it described as malicious social media posts created using AI.“We caution against such malicious posts on social media platforms which use AI to create fake content!” the ministry’s Fact Check wing said.The claim surfaced after Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, which seeks to deepen military and security cooperation among the three countries. Pakistan has described the agreement as a collective-deterrence arrangement, with its foreign ministry saying an armed attack on any one of the three signatories would be treated as an attack on all three.The agreement has drawn attention in New Delhi, with the MEA saying India is closely monitoring developments.“We are also closely following this development, and we shall keep you updated,” MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said at the ministry’s weekly briefing.The MEA’s clarification came a day after Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke by phone with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.The two leaders discussed ways to further strengthen the India-Israel Special Strategic Partnership and reviewed cooperation between the two countries across several areas.The conversation focused on strengthening bilateral ties and the existing partnership between India and Israel, rather than any new defence pact linked to the Pakistan-Saudi-Turkey agreement.
Article Summary: Mea has dismissed as “fake news” a report claiming india sought a defence pact with israel after the pakistan-saudi-turkey security agreement. The report claimed that new delhi had initiated discussions with tel aviv to counter the emerging security arrangement. The ministry called the claim “ fake news’ generated using artificial intelligence.

Article Title: Air India salary hikes salaries of pilots by up to 15%
Article Text:
Air India is restoring international flights that were slashed post the West Asia crisis and will return to Jan-Feb levels next month

NEW DELHI: Air India on Friday hiked pilot salaries by 8% to 15%, with commanders getting the biggest hikes and increases tapering by rank. Going ahead, first officers or co-pilots will get command upgrades in AI Express, which has single-aisle aircraft, then move to AI, which has wide-body aircraft with higher pay, to build progression within the group. Air India has tried to make Air India Express more attractive through better pay and to address shortages on the B737 fleet.Air India pilots have for years been facing a 40-hour guaranteed pay — meaning they get minimum pay for these hours irrespective of actual flying, while flying more means more pay — while IndiGo has fixed pay for 70 hours. Under the revised framework, Air India will continue to provide guaranteed pay for 40 flying hours but has enhanced flying allowance rates. Rates beyond 40 hours have been increased, aligning compensation with industry benchmarks while rewarding productivity.Air India is restoring international flights that were slashed post the West Asia crisis and will return to Jan-Feb levels next month. Pakistan airspace closure means longer routes, higher flying time and greater pilot requirements.A senior commander flying 55 hours a month will get Rs 8.3 lakh, up from Rs 7.5 lakh, while a first officer will get Rs 3.3 lakh, up from just over Rs 3 lakh.Privilege leave has been reduced from 30 to 24 days, though weekly offs will not be counted as leave.Since Tata Group took over Air India and Air India Express in Jan 2022, it has grown from around 100 to 300 aircraft. Under the new framework, Air India Express will serve as the “primary pathway” for command upgrades. They can then progress to Air India for wide-body flying. A fleet allowance is being offered to pilots supporting the B737 fleet in Air India Express.
Article Summary: Air india has tried to make air india express more attractive through better pay and to address shortages on the b737 fleet. Pakistan airspace closure means longer routes, higher flying time and greater pilot requirements. Air india is restoring international flights that were slashed post the west asia crisis and will return to jan-feb levels next month.

Article Title: Share data on river waters, India tells China
Article Text:
The 36th meeting of the Working Mechanism for Consultation & Coordination on India-China Border Affairs (WMCC) on Thursday saw both sides agreeing to continue using existing diplomatic and military channels

NEW DELHI: In another round of diplomatic engagement on the border issue, India and China had “frank discussions” and reviewed the situation along the line of actual control (LAC), with the former underlining that maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas is essential for the development of bilateral relations.The Indian side also reiterated the need for early convening of the next meeting of the Expert Level Mechanism on trans-border rivers, which was established in 2006, and emphasised the importance of sharing technical details on upstream projects.Following the recent announcement of a mega dam project by China, India has been raising the need for transparency and consultation with downstream countries on such upstream activities.According to the Indian govt, as a lower riparian state with established user rights to the waters of trans-border rivers, India routinely conveys its views and concerns to the Chinese authorities, and has urged them to ensure that the interests of downstream states are not harmed by activities in upstream areas. India has repeatedly stressed resumption of the provision of hydrological data and other cooperation pertaining to trans-border rivers.The 36th meeting of the Working Mechanism for Consultation & Coordination on India-China Border Affairs (WMCC) on Thursday saw both sides agreeing to continue using existing diplomatic and military channels, including the WMCC, local commander-level meetings and other agreed mechanisms, to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the LAC.An Indian readout also said that as a follow up to the outcomes of the 24th Special Representative talks on the boundary question last year, the two sides held detailed exchanges on issues related to boundary delimitation, border management, mechanism-building and trans-border cooperation.During SR talks, both sides had agreed to setting up an Expert Group, under WMCC, to explore Early Harvest in boundary delimitation in the India-China border areas. They had agreed to advance effective border management to maintain peace and tranquillity in respective border areas.
Article Summary: The 36th meeting of the working mechanism for consultation & coordination on india-china border affairs (wmcc) on thursday saw both sides agreeing to continue using existing diplomatic and military channels. Both sides agreed to advance effective border management to maintain peace and tranquillity in respective border areas.

Article Title: Tribunal reforms bill gets nod, paves way for national body
Article Text:
Minister of state for parliamentary affairs L Murugan informed the Rajya Sabha on Friday that the bill will be introduced in the Lok Sabha.

NEW DELHIL: The Cabinet on Thursday approved the Tribunals Reforms Bill that will have the provision for setting up a National Tribunal Commission (NTC), which has been visualised as an independent body to supervise appointments and functioning of around 16 tribunals and look after their administrative and infrastructural needs.Minister of state for parliamentary affairs L Murugan informed the Rajya Sabha on Friday that the bill will be introduced in the Lok Sabha. TOI has learnt that NTC will be headed by a retired SC or high court judge for five years or till he or she turns 70 years.People aware of the proposal said the government has proposed the body at the instance of the Supreme Court The apex court had ordered the constitution of NTC first in May 2018. It reiterated its directive in 2020. In November last year, SC stressed that the government has a constitutional obligation to establish NTC and gave it four months to constitute the commission, and lamented that its directions had not been heeded.In June, the Supreme Court expressed serious concern over the functioning of tribunals across the country, with CJI Surya Kant observing that these bodies have become "a liability for the judiciary" and "a headache" for the government.The CJI had said, "Tribunals were created by you (government). So it is your headache and a liability for us. Because now the kind of orders we are seeing, barring a few tribunals, these tribunals have become a no man's land. They are not accountable to anyone."
Article Summary: The cabinet on thursday approved the tribunals reforms bill. The bill will have the provision for setting up a national tribunal commission. Ntc has been visualised as an independent body to supervise appointments and functioning of around 16 tribunals.

Article Title: ‘Little hope of tracing 2 missing sailors’, Centre informs Supreme Court
Article Text:
Solicitor general (SG) Tushar Mehta told the bench that despite intense search and rescue operations, the missing Indian seafarers — Deepak Kumar Gupta and Ram Chandra Dubey — could not be located

NEW DELHI: The government informed the Supreme Court on Friday that there is very little hope of locating two Indian seafarers who are missing since the drone attack on Palau-flagged merchant ship M V AGN Ragnar on July 25 while it was departing Ukrainian waters.Filing a combined action-taken report by MEA and the Directorate General of Maritime Administration, solicitor general (SG) Tushar Mehta told the bench that despite intense search and rescue operations, the missing Indian seafarers — Deepak Kumar Gupta and Ram Chandra Dubey — could not be located.The Supreme Court told Mehta to facilitate the families’ availing maritime insurance payments.

Solicitor general (sg) tushar mehta told the bench that despite intense search and rescue operations, the missing indian seafarer — deepak kumar gupta and ram chandra dubey — could not be located.

Article Title: India’s crude import bill up 26% in ’26-27 Q1 despite 18% volume fall
Article Text:
Russia, India's biggest supplier during the quarter, supplied crude at an average cost of $2,408 per tonne, while UAE crude cost $2,213 per tonne

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India's crude import bill rose 26% year-on-year in the first quarter of 2026-27, despite volumes falling 18%, as the West Asia conflict disrupted supplies and pushed up oil prices.Commerce department data showed India imported 59.7 million tonnes (MT) of crude between April and June this year, down from 73 MT in the corresponding period last fiscal. Import bill, however, rose to $49 billion from $39 billion in April-June 2025.India is the world's third-largest crude importer, with imports meeting 88% of annual consumption. Global oil prices, which were below $70 per barrel before the US-Iran conflict broke out in Feb, surged after shipments through the Strait of Hormuz - which handles a fifth of global oil transit - were disrupted. Around 40% of India's crude imports came through the strait from West Asian suppliers. Brent crude touched nearly $120 per barrel at the conflict's peak. The weakening rupee also added to the import bill.Since India imports 1.8-2 billion barrels of crude a year, every $1-per-barrel increase in oil prices can add up to $2 billion to its oil import bill.Average cost of crude sourced from different countries varied, partly because of differences in freight, insurance and war-risk premiums.Russia, India's biggest supplier during the quarter, supplied crude at an average cost of $2,408 per tonne, while UAE crude cost $2,213 per tonne."Our priority at that time was to secure supplies from wherever possible to ensure energy security for 1.4 billion people," said an executive of a state-run refining company, adding that discounts available before the conflict had disappeared and refiners were forced to pay hefty war-risk premiums.Russia remained India's top crude supplier in the first quarter of FY27, accounting for more than 40% of imports. UAE (14.6%), Saudi Arabia (9.9%), Venezuela (5.2%) and Oman (4.5%) were the other major suppliers.
Article Summary: India is the world's third-largest crude importer, with imports meeting 88% of annual consumption. Russia remained india's top crude supplier in the first quarter of fy27, accounting for more than 40% of imports. Uae (14.6%), saudi arabia (9.9%), venezuela (5.2%) and oman were the other major suppliers.

Article Title: Past tense, eye on future: Air India hikes pilots’ pay by 8% to 15%
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Air India on Friday hiked pilot salaries by 8% to 15%, with commanders getting the biggest hikes and then the same tapering with rank. Going ahead, first officers or co-pilots will primarily get command upgrade (become captains) in AI Express (which has only single aisles) and then move to AI (which has wide body aircraft too that have higher pay) for a “strong foundation for progression within the group”. The group has tried to do multiple things — make AI Express more attractive for pilots through better pay and address shortage there mainly on the Boeing 737 fleet; check resignations and retain cockpit crew.AI pilots have for years been facing a 40 hour guaranteed pay — meaning they will get minimum for these many hours irrespective of actual flying and flying more will for more pay — while IndiGo has fixed pay for 70 hours. This has been a cause of heartburn among pilots. Under the revised framework while AI will continue to provide guaranteed pay for 40 flying hours but has enhanced flying allowance rates. Flying allowance rates beyond 40 hours have also been increased, aligning compensation with industry benchmarks while rewarding productivity.Now AI is restoring international flights that were slashed post the West Asia crisis and will return to Jan-Feb level by next month.The constraint of Pakistan airspace closure remains for Indian carriers and the longer routes they have to take for flying to and from the west — unlike direct routes taken by foreign carriers — means higher flying time and greater pilot requirement.Now a senior commander flying for about 55 hours in a month will get Rs 8.3 lakh, up from Rs 7.5 lakh at present. And a first officer doing so will get Rs 3.3 lakh, up from just over Rs 3 lakh as of now.While privilege leave has been reduced from 30 to 24, the airline will not be counting mandatory weekly off time pilots get as per regulatory requirement and the new leave structure accounts does not factor that which comes across as a cut in leave, said people in the know. IndiGo may relook at its leave policy too for pilots.Since Tata Group took over AI and AI Express in Jan 2022, the Maharaja has lost over Rs 55,000 crore due to multiple factors. The pilot pay hike announced Friday indicates it is looking at the future and preparing for growth with hundreds of aircraft on order without being bogged down by the tumultuous recent past.“New career pathways, enhanced compensation and benefits, and improved quality-of-life initiatives support Air India Group's next phase of expansion. At the heart of these initiatives is a clear, structured and transparent career pathway that provides faster command opportunities, long-term progression and access to one of the most significant widebody growth programmes in global aviation,” said an official.Since 2022, AI Group has grown from around 100 aircraft to nearly 300 aircraft and has placed orders for 600 new aircraft, including 80 wide body aircraft. Tatas are investing in capability building, including the establishment of a modern aviation academy in Gurugram with Airbus and Boeing full-flight simulators, and a new flying training school in Amravati, Maharashtra.“As AI group expands, it is focused on developing and retaining internal talent through a structured progression model across Air India Express and Air India. Pilots across Air India and Air India Express will operate under a common seniority framework, creating an integrated and transparent pathway for career progression across the group. This framework provides greater visibility into future opportunities while ensuring a consistent and structured approach to advancement,” said teh official.Under the new framework, AI Express will serve as “the primary pathway for pilots seeking command upgrades. This approach is designed to accelerate command opportunities, enable pilots to build command experience earlier in their careers, and create a strong foundation for progression within the Group.”Following command experience at AI Express, pilots will have the opportunity to progress to Air India and subsequently pursue widebody flying and command opportunities. “With 80 additional widebody aircraft on order and scheduled for induction over the coming years, Air India offers pilots a long-term pathway that is unique in the Indian market,” the official said. An additional incentive is being offered to pilots who sign up to support the growing Boeing 737 fleet in Air India Express under which they will receive a fleet allowance.
Article Summary: Commanders get the biggest hikes and then the same tapering with rank. First officers or co-pilots will primarily get command upgrade (become captains) in ai express. Article Title: India’s first satellite-guided chopper approached launched at HAL airport
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: HAL Airport in Bengaluru has become the first airport in India to operationalise a satellite-guided helicopter approach procedure, a move expected to improve safety, reduce flight times and enable more reliable all-weather operations.“The Required Navigation Performance Category H (RNP CAT H) approach, developed by the Airports Authority of India (AAI), is designed exclusively for helicopters. The procedure was validated through flight trials by HAL test pilots and approved by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA),” HAL said Friday.The new approach, it added, enables helicopters to fly highly accurate, optimised flight paths using satellite-based navigation, allowing them to safely negotiate terrain and urban obstacles while operating in adverse weather conditions.According to HAL, the procedure cuts the approach time to HAL Airport from around 12 minutes to about 4 minutes.“The operationalisation of India’s first RNP CAT H helicopter approach is a significant milestone for the country’s aviation ecosystem. This capability enhances the safety, efficiency and accessibility of helicopter operations and establishes a benchmark for similar procedures to be implemented at airports across the country,” HAL chairman and managing director Ravi K said.Besides improving safety, the system is expected to enhance operational efficiency and airspace capacity by allowing smoother integration of helicopter and fixed-wing aircraft movements. It also reduces the noise footprint over urban areas by enabling more precise flight paths.The faster approach routes are expected to benefit time-critical operations such as air ambulance services and search-and-rescue missions. HAL Airport, which handles nearly 50 helicopter movements every day, is one of the country’s busiest helicopter hubs. The introduction of the RNP CAT H procedure addresses a long-standing gap in India’s aviation infrastructure and could serve as a model for similar helicopter navigation procedures at other airports.
Article Summary: Hal airport in bengaluru has become the first airport in india to operationalise a satellite-guided helicopter approach procedure. The move is expected to improve safety, reduce flight times and enable more reliable all-weather operations. Hal airport, which handles nearly 50 helicopter movements every day, is one of the country's busiest helicopter hubs.

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Friday said that the India "had no role to play" in the recent media interaction made by former Bangladesh prime minister Sheikh Hasina In a bi-weekly press briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that event was organised by a private entity and the government does not endorse anything said at the forum."The government had no role to play in what was an event by a private media entity." Jaiswal said."It does not endorse anything said at the forum, especially with regard to the duly constituted government of Bangladesh," he added.This comes days after Hasina, during a press conference, declared that she was determined to return to Bangladesh in December to put the country on the "right track" by restoring democracy despite the possibility of imprisonment or a death sentence."I know, they may put me in jail or kill me. I will go back home to be with my people," Hasina said."Whatever fate awaits me, I will return to my people. I cannot stay away while my beloved countrymen are suffering," she said.Hasina alleged that the July-August 2024 protests that led to the fall of her government were not a spontaneous student movement but were orchestrated by organised groups to create a path to power outside the electoral process.Reacting strongly to the media interaction, Bangladesh's foreign ministry said it was "outraged" that the event had been allowed despite Dhaka raising concerns with New Delhi over its potential impact on bilateral ties."Bangladesh is outraged that the absconding convicted genocider Sheikh Hasina was allowed this evening to engage in a live interaction with the media in New Delhi, where she and her henchmen launched venomous vitriol against the State of Bangladesh and its people," the ministry said in a statement.Describing the event as "an affront to the sovereignty of Bangladesh", the ministry alleged that Hasina and her associates had used Indian soil to launch "venomous vitriol" against Bangladesh and its people.Reiterating its position, the foreign ministry said Bangladesh remained committed to building a constructive and mutually beneficial relationship with India based on sovereign equality, mutual respect, non-interference and national dignity.Dhaka also urged India to clarify its policy towards Bangladesh.Bangladesh's state minister for foreign affairs Shama Obaed said New Delhi must decide whether it would continue to allow Awami League leaders to "carry out conspiratorial activities" from its territory."India is a democratic country. India itself has to decide what its foreign policy will be regarding Bangladesh. We want good relations in the interest of the people of both countries," she said."But the relationship has to be based on equality, mutual respect and safeguarding each country's interests. If India understands that, it will be good for everyone," she added.
Article Summary: Mea spokesperson randhir jaiswal said that event was organised by a private entity and the government does not endorse anything said at the forum. Bangladesh's foreign ministry said it was "outraged" that the event had been allowed despite dhaka raising concerns with new delhi.

NEW DELHI: Ministry of external affairs on Friday rejected criticism of India's foreign funding law, saying the issue is an internal matter on which Parliament will take a decision.During a bi-weekly media briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said several countries, including the United States, regulate foreign funds and foreign financing."Regarding the issue you are referring to, we have seen it, and several comments have been made on it. As far as legislative matters are concerned, and particularly matters relating to India's own legislation, this is an internal matter for us, on which our Parliament takes the decision," Jaiswal said."I would also like to tell you that there are several countries in the world, including the United States, that regulate foreign funds and foreign financing," he added.The remarks came days after a US lawmaker criticised the proposed amendments to India's foreign funding law, alleging they could allow the government to take over churches and religious charities and warning that the issue could affect India-US ties.Also read: Monsoon Session: Congress issues whip to MPs ahead of FCRA Bill discussion in Parliament US Congressman Riley Moore said the proposed changes to the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA) amounted to "a clear attack against Christians" and urged India not to proceed with the legislation in its current form.In a post on X, the Republican Congressman from West Virginia said Christianity had a long history in India dating back to the arrival of St Thomas the Apostle on the Malabar Coast."But despite this long Christian history, India's Parliament is considering amending the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act to permit government takeovers of churches and religious charities," Moore wrote."This is a clear attack against Christians. If this bill proceeds in this way, it would be a point of major concern in our bilateral relationship with India," he added.The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 proposes the creation of a Designated Authority to take over the management of foreign contributions and assets created using such funds if an organisation's FCRA registration is cancelled, surrendered or lapses after not being renewed.The Bill specifies that where such assets include a place of worship, the Designated Authority must ensure its religious character is preserved.It also proposes reducing the maximum punishment for violations of the Act from five years' imprisonment to one year.The FCRA regulates the receipt and utilisation of foreign contributions by NGOs, charitable trusts, educational institutions, religious bodies and other associations. According to the Ministry of Home Affairs, 13,520 organisations received foreign contributions worth Rs 55,741 crore between 2019 and 2022.Government data shows that as of July 15, 2026, there were 14,449 active FCRA registrations, while 22,498 had been cancelled and another 15,212 had expired.

Article Title: Former Nestle CMD Suresh Narayanan says India Inc needs to shed the ‘elite’ tag
Article Text:
Former Nestle CMD Suresh Narayanan in his new book, 'Courage Under Fire', writes that in a crisis people follow those they trust.

For over four decades,

Suresh Narayanan

has navigated boardrooms, brand battles and one of

India Inc

's defining crises. In ‘

Courage Under Fire

’ (

Penguin Random House India

), the former Nestlé India chairman and managing director looks beyond business strategy to explore what truly shapes

leadership

.

In an exclusive chat with Lopamudra Ghatak, he argues that clarity matters more than charisma, challenges India's obsession with pedigree that’s causing companies to overlook leadership potential, and reflects candidly on the lessons of the

Maggi

crisis. He also explains why

Gen Z

's approach to work-life balance deserves respect rather than ridicule, and recalls how a woman boss taught him that empathy is one of the key traits to being a good leader.

Congratulations on your book. How did the idea to write 'Courage Under Fire' come to you?

In 'Courage Under Fire' you write that "great leadership is not about position; it’s about responsibility, authenticity, and the ability to inspire trust, when it matters". In an increasingly trust-deficit and information-surplus world, how does a leader earn trust? And how does an organisation make trust a part of its DNA?

leadership. You mention in the book about visiting Tier-2 and Tier3- colleges, and how students there are often more grateful, hungry and eager to learn. Do you think they make better leaders?

You have spent over four decades across big brands. Do you think India Inc has begun to move beyond that elitism?

The modern workplace has become very volatile, with geopolitics and global uncertainty adding new layers of complexity. What's your advice for leaders navigating crises?

You also had a woman boss during your career. Did her leadership style differ from your male mentors?

Gen Z and the emerging Gen Alpha are reshaping workplace expectations as they place a premium on work-life balance, purpose and flexibility. How do you see that influencing India's workforce in the years ahead?

After a 40-year career in corporate India, I wanted to leave behind a few lessons that had served me well. They're not prescriptions, but perspectives shaped by the crises and difficult moments I have experienced.'Courage Under Fire' is more of a personal journey through those defining moments - that focuses on people, purpose, partnerships, values, behaviour and outcomes. I thought it would be of some use to a younger generation entering the workforce.I think you've hit the nail on the head! Trust is the most valuable currency - for an individual as much as for an organisation. It emerges when three streams converge at one point in time.The first is purpose. Every organisation, and every individual, needs a clear sense of purpose, something that guides decisions and actions.The second is values. What do you want to be known for? What principles define how you conduct yourself, especially in adverse situations?Purpose and values, in turn, lead to the third element: authenticity. Unfortunately, in today's digital world, authenticity often gives way to performance.We spend too much time embellishing, instead of being genuine.Correct. Leadership isn't about saying what you'll do, it's about doing what you say. That's the dilemma many leaders face. Do they wear a(mask) that projects one image while concealing another?In order to establish trust among people, there has to be a convergence between purpose, values and authenticity, and that leads to outcomes. Over time, those actions create credibility, and credibility becomes trust.Trust is built when purpose, values and authenticity consistently translate into action. Over time, those actions create credibility, and credibility becomes trust.I've also come to see vulnerability as a strength, not a weakness. When people know you're human, that you have strengths as well as limitations, they know what to expect from you. Predictability in values and behaviour is reassuring. What people fear most is unpredictability.Ultimately, trust isn't about being the most liked person in the room. In a crisis, organisations don't rely on the most loved people; they rely on the most trusted ones. If I'm liked but not trusted, I won't be asked to lead when it matters. Trust, more than popularity, is what carries an organisation through difficult times.Leadership, for long, has suffered from some myths. The first is the myth of charisma - that great leaders must have magnetic personalities. The second is that complex communication (by leadership) is somehow superior. The third is executive presence: the belief that a leader must be a larger-than-life figure at any gathering and dominate every room they enter. And the fourth is the idea that leaders should only display their strengths while hiding every flaw, angularities.I don't subscribe to any of those myths. Leadership can absolutely be taught because, at its core, leadership is an act of being human.You don't have to be charismatic; you have to be clear. You don't have to be complex; you have to be transparent in your communication. You don't need the loudest voice or the most commanding presence. Some of history's greatest political and business leaders inspired people far beyond the reach of their voices.But leadership doesn't develop in isolation. It blooms through the right mentors, timely nudges and experiences. Looking back, I benefited from teachers, parents, colleagues, relatives and even competitors who pushed me to exceed my own expectations. Those influences gradually built confidence, not just the confidence to lead others, but the confidence to manage myself first.One thing we need to do as a society is demystify elitism. We place far too much value on where someone studied, where they work, the company they built or the organisation they belong to — as though those labels alone define success and achievement.Exactly, the tag culture. I believe those days should be behind us. Look at ISRO. They might have their own travails but the fact is that most of the talent that comes there are not from the premier institutions in the country and yet they do premier and outstanding work and make us proud as a nation.The same is true of organisations that consciously recruit from Tier-2 cities and smaller towns. I often find students there to be remarkably humble, eager and determined. They are trying to prove themselves against a system that has long suggested only the elite succeed.As leaders, we have to move away from that entitlement mindset and create space for talent to flourish. India has extraordinary talent. Some young people may not be the most articulate when speaking in English but they are capable of hard work and possess grit, discipline and can deliver on their promise each and every time.That's what the country needs—not people who merely preach from the pulpit, but people who consistently deliver.I think as a country now we are mature enough to realise that we cannot be a developing country or hope to become a wealthy country one day on the crutches of elitism. I think elitism is a crutch that we have to get out of as quickly as possible.I think the kind of companies that I worked in - Unilever, Colgate-Palmolive and Nestle - they always prided themselves in a middle-class culture. Their leaders weren't chosen because they came from privileged backgrounds; they rose through competence, commitment, energy and hard workI use the term middle class in a positive sense because it symbolises humility, integrity, transparency, trust and a strong work ethic. This is what middle-class India is, and these are the values we strive to teach our children. When those values enter an organisation, they become a source of strength.I do think the growing recognition of talent from Tier-2 institutions and smaller towns is slowly weakening elitism. But there's still work to be done. Our education system and employers must create more opportunities for capable graduates from less celebrated institutions.Too many people still believe admission to a top college guarantees success. Life doesn't work that way. Success is usually about moving two steps forward, one step back, and repeating that journey with resilience and consistency.There are two principles that have guided me throughout my career.The first is simple: a crisis never arrives with a calling card. You have to remain alert at all times. Don't be caught sleeping at the wheel. Anticipate risks before they balloon into crises.The second is to manage yourself before you manage others. That's often overlooked. When a crisis hits, we immediately focus on facts, meetings and firefighting. But we spend far less time asking:In a crisis, everyone's anxiety levels are elevated. The leader's role is to remain calm, anchored in the organisation's purpose and values, and provide stability.That's often the difference between a crisis handled well and one handled badly. The outcome rarely depends only on strategy. More often, it depends on leadership—how clearly you communicate, how consistently you act and how much confidence you inspire.The first lesson, that a crisis doesn't come with a calling card, certainly applies in this case. In hindsight, we could have done better in terms of sensing the environment and knowing that something was brewing in parts of the country. If we had been able to address it more comprehensively, maybe we would have been able to manage the outcome a lot better.Secondly, one of the important issues in managing a crisis is to have a single point of contact communicating to the environment. One criticism we faced was that we were slow in communicating. Looking back, I believe we could have responded faster.I don't know whether the dial has shifted enough in India to say that with confidence. But I do believe people follow leaders who are authentic, humane and emotionally present — not those who remain distant and issue instructions from above.Professor George Kohlrieser at IMD Business School describes a leader as a "secure base." I find that idea deeply meaningful. Just as we turn to a parent in moments of uncertainty, employees should feel they have someone they can approach with their fears, concerns and aspirations, someone who will provide anchorage in a crisis.Vulnerability, to me, is a source of strength. It acknowledges that you're still learning and growing. That's not weakness, it's humanity.We've long been told that men don't cry. But they do. Suppressing emotion doesn't make you stronger; it makes it harder to empathise. And empathy is one of the most powerful qualities a leader can possess.Wan Ling, who headed Nestle Asia-Oceania-Africa, was one of the toughest leaders I worked with. She could be incredibly demanding, yet deeply compassionate.What struck me most was that every conversation with her began with family. With many of my male bosses, business came first and family last. With her it was always, “How is your family doing?”. Only then would we move on to tackle the toughest business crisis moments.One of her greatest strengths was her ability to read a room. She sensed what people were feeling before anyone uttered a word. Just as importantly, she had the ability to step back, consider various perspectives and avoid rushing into decisions. That balance of empathy and judgement made her an exceptional leader.I see it as a positive shift. The old belief that success demanded 80-hour work weeks came at a huge personal cost. You may have earned more, but you often missed out on family, friendships and life's important moments. There's little value in reaching 80 and regretting that you never spent enough time with your parents or your children. So I welcome this change.These youngsters are not work-shy. They simply want work to coexist with life, and I think that's a healthy aspiration. I only wish my generation had the courage to tell our bosses at seven in the evening that we were leaving to meet family or friends. Instead, we stayed back until the boss switched off the lights, as though commitment was measured by the last person to leave the office.That said, balance has to be calibrated. Every generation has something to learn from the other.What also strikes me about young professionals is that they're driven by experiences. They move from one challenge to another in search of learning and fulfillment. I would encourage them to embrace the challenge itself rather than becoming overly anxious about the outcome. Careers are rarely linear. If you focus on learning, growth and doing meaningful work, the outcomes usually take care of themselves.
Article Summary: Former nestle cmd suresh narayanan writes that in a crisis people follow those they trust. He argues that clarity matters more than charisma and challenges india's obsession with pedigree. He also explains why gen z's approach to work-life balance deserves respect rather than ridicule.

Article Title: Any post against PM Modi to be deleted in three hours: Arvind Kejriwal on new social media law
Article Text:
Kejriwal slams Centre's new social media law

NEW DELHI: Aam Aadmi Party supremo Arvind Kejriwal on Friday launched a sharp attack on the Centre over its newly introduced social media law, alleging that it is aimed at silencing criticism of the government and reflects Prime Minister Narendra Modi's growing fear of public protests.Addressing supporters, former Delhi CM Kejriwal claimed the new law would require social media platforms to take down any post flagged by the government within three hours."The Modi government has introduced a new law. If the government asks any social media platform, whether Instagram, Facebook or any other platform, to delete a post or video, it will have to be removed within three hours," he said.He alleged that the provision would be used to target posts critical of the government on issues such as paper leaks, the ethanol policy and corruption, while allowing abusive content from its supporters to remain online."If you speak against Modi ji, the government, paper leaks, the ethanol issue or corruption, your post will be deleted within three hours. But if people associated with them use abusive language or target women, no action is taken against such content," he alleged.AAP chief Kejriwal further claimed that Prime Minister Modi has become increasingly anxious after recent youth-led protests and demonstrations at Jantar Mantar."Modi ji fears the people of this country. He fears the youth, children and women. Ever since the protests at Jantar Mantar, he has been gripped by fear," Kejriwal alleged.Arguing that censorship cannot substitute governance, the former Delhi chief minister said silencing criticism would only deepen public resentment."The solution is not to silence people's voices. If the government does good work, people will praise it on their own. The public has no personal enmity with anyone. But if you suppress criticism instead of addressing people's concerns, public anger will only grow," he said.Kejriwal also warned that governments that fear their own citizens eventually lose public support."The days of a ruler who fears his own people are numbered. The more you try to suppress the voices of the people, the stronger their anger will become," he said.Earlier to this, Kejriwal also claimed that Meta restricted his account and slammed Mark Zuckerberg-led social media giant.
Article Summary: Kejriwal slams centre's new social media law. Former delhi cm claims the new law would require social media platforms to take down any post flagged by the government within three hours. He alleged that the provision would be used to target posts critical of the government on issues such as paper leaks, the ethanol policy and corruption.

Article Title: Iran officials 'would not be surprised' if Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei dies soon: Report
Article Text:
Mojtaba Khamenei in 'extremely critical condition', may die soon, Iranian sources say​

Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei ’s health has come under renewed scrutiny after IranWire, citing two sources close to President Masoud Pezeshkian’s administration, reported that senior officials are increasingly concerned about his condition.According to IranWire, Khamenei has not met any cabinet members since the February 28 US-Israeli strikes that killed his father and predecessor, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, along with other members of his family. The outlet said rumours that the younger Khamenei is in an “extremely critical condition” and could die soon are circulating within Iran’s highest levels of government.One source close to the Pezeshkian administration told IranWire that Khamenei’s physical condition was poor, adding that officials “would not be surprised” if they soon heard news of his death.The claims have not been independently verified. Iranian authorities have not announced that Khamenei is critically ill, while reports circulating in Israeli media have also claimed that he was recently taken to hospital. These reports cite Iranian sources but have not provided independent evidence of his current condition.Also read: Iran President met a 'voice in the dark', isn't sure it was Mojtaba Khamenei: Report The speculation has been amplified by Khamenei’s unusually low public profile since taking over as supreme leader.He has made no public appearances or televised speeches since assuming the position, with Iranian state media publishing only written statements attributed to him.That absence has led to repeated questions about his health and ability to govern, particularly after reports that he was injured in the February strike that killed his father.Iranian officials have previously disputed reports that his injuries were severe. State-linked officials have described his injuries as limited and maintained that he remains involved in strategic decision-making.President Pezeshkian himself said in a state television interview this week that communicating with Khamenei was currently “very difficult”, adding another layer to speculation surrounding the supreme leader's condition.Separately, a report by Iran International, said Pezeshkian was taken to an undisclosed location in Tehran for a brief meeting with a man presented as Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei. According to the report, the meeting took place inside a darkened vehicle and Pezeshkian was unable to see the man’s face. He later reportedly questioned whether the voice he heard actually belonged to Khamenei.The claims come as Iran remains under intense pressure following the conflict with the US and Israel and amid difficult negotiations over the Strait of Hormuz. The Wall Street Journal reported that Pezeshkian and other officials have struggled to gain access to Khamenei, who has remained largely absent from public view.
Article Summary: Mojtaba khamenei in 'extremely critical condition', may die soon, iranian sources say. Khamenei has not met any cabinet members since the february 28 us-israeli strikes that killed his father and predecessor, ayatollah ali khamenei. Iranian authorities have not announced that khamenei is critically ill.

Article Title: 'Who introduced them?' US senator says it's odd to see Justin Trudeau frolicking around Katy Perry; 'He used to be in charge of a whole country'
Article Text:
Alabama senator says it's odd to see Justin Trudeau frolicking around Katy Perry.

Justin Trudeau and Katy Perry were recently seen in France celebrating what is being termed as their first anniversary. A Republican senator (Alabama), Katie Britt, said it's kind of odd watching the celebrity couple frolicking because Justin Trudeau led a country. "It's like, he used to be in charge of a whole country, now we sort of see him frolic," she said."But like how did he get with Katy Perry? That's actually the question we should be getting to. Like, who introduced them? Obviously they didn't find each other on an app. You know? Like, how did that go down?" she asked.The former Canadian PM and Katy Perry were first spotted together in Montreal in July 2025. In October, they were seen aboard Perry's yacht off the coast of Santa Barbara, California. They were seen hugging and kissing. During New Year's, Katy Perry posted photos with Justin Trudeau and since then, it has been one outing after another for the couple. In January 2026, the couple made their high-profile public appearances in Davos. They were seen at Coachella and then the Tribeca Film Festival, and their latest has been a French vacation."They're both complete exhibitionists when they're together," National Examiner cited a source as saying."It's probably shocking for people who know Justin from his political days.""The problem is Katy travels with this enormous entourage wherever she goes, so people are constantly having to sit there and avert their eyes," the same report said.Katy Perry ended her relationship with Orlando Bloom in June 2025 a month before she was first seen with Trudeau. Perry and Bloom are parents to six-year-old daughter Daisy Bloom. Justin Trudeau and his ex-wife Sophie Gregoire divorced in 2023 after 18 years of marriage. They have three children: Xavier, Ella-Grace and Hadrien.Doing his 'boyfriend duty', Trudeau drew flak as he attended the opening match of the FIFA World Cup in Los Angeles and skipped Canada's match."There is a long history of political powers dating or even marrying celebrities, including Senator John W Warner and Elizabeth Taylor, Senator Cory Booker and Rosario Dawson, President Nicolas Sarkozy of France and the model Carla Bruni, and Trudeau’s own father, Pierre Trudeau, and Barbra Streisand, Kim Cattrall and Margot Kidder. In most cases, though, the celebrities enter the politician’s world, remaking themselves to fit," an NYT feature on Trudeau's rebranding as a boyfriend noted.
Article Summary: Alabama senator says it's odd to see justin trudeau frolicking around katy perry. "it's like, he used to be in charge of a whole country, now we sort of see him frolic," she said. Justin trudeau and katy perry were first spotted together in montreal in july 2025.

Article Title: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan & Turkey sign 'Mecca' pact for mutual defence; India reacts
Article Text:
Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan each bring distinct strategic strengths to the partnership.

Deal amid turbulent West Asia

3 distinct strategic strengths

Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey Friday signed a trilateral defence agreement aimed at strengthening their collective security as the conflict involving Iran continues to fuel instability across the West Asia.The agreement was signed following a joint defence summit attended by Saudi crown prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish president Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Pakistani prime minister Shehbaz Sharif, who attended after performing the Umrah pilgrimage in the city.According to Pakistan's foreign ministry, the pact is "guided by the longstanding historical ties among the three states, based on the enduring bonds of brotherhood and Islamic solidarity that unite them, and building upon their shared strategic interests and longstanding defence cooperation".The agreement is intended to strengthen collective deterrence against any act of aggression and stipulates that an armed attack against any of the three would be regarded as an attack on all, they said in a joint statement.The Pakistani ministry said the agreement reflects "the three states’ shared commitment to further strengthening their collective security and to promoting peace, security, and stability in the region and beyond, in pursuit of a secure and prosperous future."Also read: Evening news wrap: CBI chargesheet alleges NTA's own experts leaked NEET-UG, MEA rejects US criticism of of FCRA Bill & more It added that "The agreement is intended to strengthen collective deterrence against any act of aggression, and stipulates that any armed attack against any one of the three states shall be regarded as an attack against them all."Meanwhile, India reacted to the development, saying "developments were closely watched".Responding to reports on the agreement, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said: “The pact between the three countries is, again, a development that we are closely following, and we will keep you updated on that.”The deal comes as Saudi Arabia and other Gulf countries continue to face missile attacks and disruptions to energy shipments amid the ongoing conflict involving Iran and its regional allies. The war escalated after the United States and Israel launched attacks on Iran on February 28, triggering a wider regional crisis.A Turkish official said the agreement was purely defensive, was not aimed at any particular country and remained open to participation by other regional nations. The official also said it would not replace any existing bilateral or multilateral security arrangements.Analysts said the summit carried significant geopolitical weight at a time of growing uncertainty in the region."The political symbolism of the summit is significant. Three of the Muslim world's most influential states are convening at a moment of heightened uncertainty, demonstrating a growing willingness among regional and middle powers to coordinate more closely on security matters," Abdulaziz Sager, chairman of the Saudi-based Gulf Research Center, told new agency Reuters."If institutionalised and translated into concrete cooperation, the trilateral framework could strengthen the three countries' collective diplomatic and defense weight while contributing to the emergence of a more regionally driven security architecture," Sager added.Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan each bring distinct strategic strengths to the partnership. Turkey has Nato's second-largest military, Saudi Arabia is one of the world's biggest oil exporters and custodian of Islam's holiest sites, while Pakistan is the only Muslim-majority country with nuclear weapons.The agreement follows months of discussions on expanding regional security cooperation. Earlier this year, Turkish foreign minister Hakan Fidan had said Ankara supported a broader regional security platform to promote stability.Experts believe the pact builds on long-standing military ties among the three countries. Pakistan has trained Saudi security forces for decades, while Turkey and Pakistan have cooperated on defence equipment and military training. Saudi Arabia also signed a major deal in 2023 to purchase Turkish drones.Mansoor Ahmed of the Australian National University's Strategic and Defence Studies Centre said Pakistan and Turkey could contribute advanced defence manufacturing capabilities, while Saudi Arabia could provide financial and technological investment.He added, however, that the new agreement was unlikely to include a nuclear component because Pakistan's nuclear deterrent remains focused on India.Pakistan has also expanded its military presence in Saudi Arabia in recent months by deploying thousands of troops, fighter aircraft, drones and air defence systems. It has simultaneously pursued broader security partnerships with Gulf countries, including talks with Kuwait on an expanded defence arrangement linked to energy cooperation and investment.
Article Summary: Saudi arabia, turkey and pakistan each bring distinct strategic strengths to the partnership. The agreement is intended to strengthen collective deterrence against any act of aggression. It stipulates that an armed attack against any of the three would be regarded as an attack on all.
